title: Consumption actions (used it up / used some / wasted) + implicit virtual depletion projection
goal: Close F9.1's explicit half of the consumption loop -- 'used it up' / 'used some' / 'wasted' actions that write real stock_movements and trigger a recompute -- on top of S-19's virtual-depletion display (F9.2), so the app is correct whether or not the household ever taps a button. This is also the story that unblocks E-5's S-15 repurchase-reconciliation loop, which has been a documented, deliberate no-op on real households since E-5 shipped, pending 'at least one real consumption/adjustment/waste movement' existing for an item (.claude/epic-5/sub-S-15.json, .claude/epic-5/ledger.md).
in_scope: lib/inventory/consume.ts (server-only): recordConsumption(catalogItemId, householdId, action, payload) -> Promise<void>. 'used_up': reads raw v_current_stock for the item; if <=0, no-op (nothing to write, already zero); else writes one stock_movements row, type='consumption', qty_base = -rawStock, occurred_at = now. 'used_some' with a preset fraction (0.25 / 0.5 / 0.75): fraction is applied to the DISPLAYED virtual stock (S-19's computeVirtualStockBase) -- what the user is actually looking at when they tap the button -- clamped so the resulting movement magnitude never exceeds raw stock (a defensive backstop; virtual <= raw always per S-19's own invariant, so this clamp should never actually bind in practice). 'used_some' with a numeric amount (entered in the item's base unit, since the card already displays base + friendly units): clamped to raw stock the same way. 'wasted': same zeroing behavior as used_up, but type='waste' instead of 'consumption' -- a distinct ledger type for F13's future waste report, which this story does not build.

After any actual write (the used-up-when-already-zero case is the only no-op), calls recomputeOneItem(catalogItemId, householdId) with no rate_correction override -- S-15's reconciliation is on-commit-purchase-only per its own invariants and is never invoked from a consumption action.

app/inventory/[id]/actions.ts ('use server') + a client component on the item detail page: three actions (Used it up / Used some / Wasted); 'Used some' opens an inline choice of 25/50/75% or a numeric base-unit input. Actions revalidatePath the item detail page, the inventory list, and '/' (the Today stub).

lib/inventory/data.ts: getItemsNeedingAttention() -- items whose virtual stock is <= 0 AND (hasStockRow OR lastPurchasedAt !== null), queried the same batched way as getInventoryItems. The hasStockRow disjunct is load-bearing, not a defensive extra: lastPurchasedAt only exists once item_stats has been computed, which only happens once a PURCHASE movement exists (recomputeOneItem no-ops on zero purchase events). An onboarding-only item (one 'initial' movement, no item_stats row) still gets a v_current_stock row the moment a consumption action writes a movement against it -- confirmed via a live query to be the majority real-world state (22/22 positive-stock items on the real household are onboarding-only, zero item_stats rows). An earlier lastPurchasedAt-only draft would have silently excluded every one of them from this list after 'Used it up' -- caught by advisor review before implementation, verified against a real onboarding-only item (not a fabricated purchase-history fixture) before this story was considered done.

app/page.tsx: a minimal 'Needs attention' section listing getItemsNeedingAttention() results, each linking to /inventory/[id] -- this is what makes A8's 'appears in Today' concretely true today. The full bucketed Today view (cadence tabs, everything due within 3 days) is E-8's S-22, which cannot exist yet (blocked_by S-21, itself blocked_by this epic + S-18) -- this addition is deliberately minimal, not a preview of S-22.
out_of_scope: The full bucketed Today view (cadence tabs, due-within-3-days across all buckets, snooze/skip) -- E-8's S-22. This story only extends the existing app/page.tsx stub with a needs-attention list.
Shopping-list checkoff logging a purchase movement (F12 / E-9) -- a different movement type and flow entirely, unrelated to consumption.

Any change to reconcile.ts's own logic or its consumption-signal gate query -- this story satisfies the gate (a real non-purchase movement now exists for items that use these actions) without touching the gate's code.
A waste report (F13 / E-12) -- the 'waste' movement type is written here so that report has data to read later, but no report is built in this story.
acceptance: "Used it up" zeroes stock and surfaces the item in Today (A8); virtual depletion never writes a ledger movement.
invariants: computeVirtualStockBase (S-19) is a pure, read-only function -- never called from consume.ts's write path to decide what to persist, and consume.ts never fabricates a movement whose source is 'the virtual projection.' Every write here is a real, user-triggered explicit action against the real ledger, matching F9.2's 'never a written ledger movement' clause for the implicit/virtual side.

A consumption or waste movement's qty_base magnitude is always <= the raw v_current_stock available at write time, WITHIN a single request -- consume.ts clamps the requested amount to the stock it itself read and skips the write entirely if the clamped amount is <=0 (covers 'used it up' tapped twice in sequence, and any fraction/amount that rounds to zero). This does NOT fully close a genuine concurrent double-submit race: two in-flight requests can both read the same pre-write rawStockBase before either commits, and both would then write against it. That residual risk is accepted and stated here rather than claimed away -- the UI disables action buttons while a request is pending as a mitigation, not a guarantee. A real fix would need an atomic DB-side check-and-write (a stored procedure, matching commit_receipt()'s precedent) and was judged out of scope for this story's actual risk level (a single-household, non-concurrent-in-practice app).
recordConsumption never touches item_stats.rate_correction directly -- only recomputeOneItem's own read-modify-persist cycle (called with no override, exactly like the nightly path) can change it.

Consumption actions never pass a rateCorrectionOverride to recomputeOneItem -- that parameter is reserved for S-15's reconcileRateCorrection output on the purchase-commit path only; reusing it here would let a 'used it up' tap corrupt rate_correction through a path S-15 was never designed to be called from.
